bottom_line: Stocks are getting hit hard. AI stocks are selling off even after Anthropic's big stock market debut, and the Fed (the people who set interest rates) keeps saying inflation is too high and more rate hikes are coming. Prices are still rising too fast, so borrowing is getting more expensive.

stories.title: AI selloff drags stocks down
stories.real: The Dow fell about 1,100 points and closed below 50,000 for the first time since June. The S&P 500 had its 6th straight day of losses, and stocks are on their worst run since 2023. Anthropic debuted at a $1.8 trillion value and soared 17% on day one, but it didn't stop the AI selloff, and it fell nearly 6% before the next day's open.

stories.title: The Fed is ready to raise rates
stories.real: Fed officials say flat out that inflation is too high. Goolsbee says it's 'way higher' than their 2% target. They're signaling more rate hikes, and J.P. Morgan expects hikes at each of the next three meetings. The officials agree rates should go up. They just disagree on how fast.
stories.you: Credit cards, car loans and mortgages will likely get more expensive to borrow on, but savings accounts may pay you a bit more.

stories.title: Gold takes a big fall
stories.real: Gold has fallen more than 30% from its January record, down near $3,500 an ounce. That's its lowest since September 2025, and gold is heading for its worst week in 8 months. Two reasons: a stronger dollar and bets that the Fed will raise rates.
stories.you: Gold isn't acting like a safe place to park money right now. If you hold it, it's lost a lot of value since January.

stories.title: Trouble at the big chipmakers
stories.real: AMD closed down over 7% after a short seller (someone who profits when a stock falls) claimed AMD's chip software turned up at a blacklisted Chinese company. AMD says it follows U.S. law. Meanwhile, California is investigating Nvidia over AI chips in China after former CEO Jensen Huang left, and the company's legal risk keeps growing.
stories.you: Many funds hold huge chunks of Nvidia and AMD, so their problems can drag down your retirement account even if you never bought them yourself.

stories.title: Regular people are getting squeezed
stories.real: According to the Fed, unless you're building data centers or have a side hustle, you're significantly worse off than last year. More cost increases are already on the way. More people are filing for unemployment, though the number is still low historically. Walmart raised its outlook and says it will try to keep prices low even with fuel costs soaring.
stories.you: Your paycheck probably isn't keeping up with prices, so expect everyday costs and borrowing to keep pinching.
